title: What I learned using AI throughout the development of my first Steam demo
author: civilizedcomics
selftext:
I’ve been building my first commercial game, **Dreadlight**, with AI incorporated into most parts of the development process. It’s a horror survivorlike with short waves, automatic weapons, build crafting, and an arena that develops persistent ritual scars during each run.

This game has taken me about 3-4 months now and I think I could do it in a fraction of that time if I started over again today.  But, iteration is what got me here and I'm pretty happy with the final result.

I used AI for programming assistance, concept development, UI iterations, visual assets, some audio work, marketing materials, and testing tools. I still made the design decisions, selected and revised the output, implemented the game, tested builds, and handled the Steam and itch setup.

The biggest lesson has been that generating something is the easy part. Consistency is the actual work.

A character image can look good by itself and still fail as a game sprite. Generated icons may use inconsistent framing or contrast. UI text can technically fit while being nearly unreadable during play. Multi-frame animation was particularly difficult because small variations in pose, proportions, and background removal became very obvious in motion. I eventually abandoned one animation attempt rather than forcing inconsistent assets into the demo.

It can become incredibly frustrating trying to fine tune a UI where it doesn't exactly understand what I'm trying to tell it.  Also trying to get it to do animation frames was a nightmare.  It was really bad at lining up each frame so they would jump around all over the place.

The game now has a public demo. I’m interested in feedback from other AI-assisted developers, especially around maintaining visual consistency and deciding when generated work needs manual cleanup or should simply be discarded.

Itch Demo: [https://thebeesknees13.itch.io/dreadlight-demo](https://thebeesknees13.itch.io/dreadlight-demo)

Steam Page: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5003470/Dreadlight/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5003470/Dreadlight/)

I’m also happy to discuss the parts of the workflow that worked, the parts that absolutely did not.

replies.body: I have, I have a sub for it actually, but I found it wasn't getting me where I wanted with the animations.  A lot of them still had some jank where I felt like the single sprites worked better

replies.body: It doesn’t do a great job with sheets, no. But I agree it’s pretty decent at individual sprites
